findings.title: The invocation frames the oath and verdict
findings.claim: The basmala's naming act gathers the following oath and verdict under the invoked name, so the sequence reads as an authorized warning-and-rescue utterance.
findings.mechanism: At the focus, bi-ism names Allah: the proper divine name and the word of designation are already present. The next context unit swears by time, then 103:2 states loss and 103:3 specifies an exception. This name-before-oath contact lets the initial formula govern the reading of the compressed verdict; the basmala itself is not the oath.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening is heard as an operative invocation within the surah's warning-and-rescue sequence rather than as a detachable title.
findings.containment: Allah remains the named divine referent and the focus remains an invocation. The authorization is an inferred speech-force relation between the opening and the following sequence; it does not make the basmala sworn speech or claim that the syntax explicitly attributes the later utterances to the invoked name.

epistemic.reason: A trusted published finding supports the two-branch relation and the ordered surah surface supplies the oath and verdict; legacy reader walks agree, while the procedural arrow from invocation to authorization remains inferential.

findings.title: Mercy frames the diagnosis and exception
findings.claim: The two mercy titles frame the diagnosis of loss and the exception's path out as beneficence; the sequence invites a rescue-from-mercy reading, while leaving its causal arrow unstated.
findings.mechanism: The focus repeats the mercy root in two divine adjectives before 103:2 places humanity in loss and 103:3 describes the exception through belief, good work, and reciprocal exhortation. This fronted-mercy-to-later-exit contact makes the route read within benevolence rather than as a detached moral checklist, though the text does not explicitly state that mercy causes those conditions.
findings.reader_payoff: The severe diagnosis and the conditions of escape remain together inside a frame of beneficence.
findings.containment: This adds a mercy-frame to the stated meanings of loss, belief, work, truth, and patience; it does not replace those meanings or assert an explicit causal claim that the verses do not make.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication and reader-walk evidence support the framing relation. The sequence itself is present, but the arrow from preposed mercy to enabled rescue is identified by the reader walk as abductive.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: The two focus adjectives name God's mercy as an active movement toward beneficence; the primary gloss remains mercy.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The next two context units present humanity's loss and the exception's described path out through belief, good deeds, and mutual exhortation.
branch_activations.activation: The opening mercy carrier meets the later contrast between loss and the exception. Because the branch contains active sparing and goodness, the route out is heard as lying within offered beneficence rather than as a detached sequence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The diagnosis and exception are framed as a rescue offered within mercy.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch does not prove that mercy is the explicit grammatical cause of the exception or that belief and work are merely effects of mercy.

findings.title: Reciprocal exhortation makes the kinship image social
findings.claim: The doubled mercy names at the entrance resonate with the repeated mutual exhortation in the exception, so the saved group can be heard as a kinship-like reciprocal bond.
findings.mechanism: The focus repeats the r-h-m carrier, while 103:3 repeats tawasaw among the plural exception-community. The kinship branch contacts this independent reciprocal act: the opening's repeated mercy takes on a communal relation-shape instead of remaining only an attribute over the passage.
findings.reader_payoff: The rescued group becomes perceptible as a mutually held community rather than a set of isolated individuals.
findings.containment: The focus words remain divine mercy titles, and the later group is not claimed to share literal ancestry. Kinship is an attributed analogy made by the structural contact, not a lexical replacement.

epistemic.reason: The repeated focus and context structures are supplied directly, and a trusted published finding records the relation; kinship-like social organization is still an interpretive analogy.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The exception-community reads as linked by a durable, kinship-like mutual bond.
branch_activations.boundary: No genealogical relation or literal kinship is asserted; the analogy does not replace the meaning of mercy.

findings.title: The womb branch counters being inside loss
findings.claim: The womb branch carried by the opening mercy can serve as a life-bearing counter-image to the statement that humanity is in loss, while the exception gives that image an exit-shaped context.
findings.mechanism: The focus mercy adjectives share the r-h-m root carrier with the womb branch. The later fī khusr construction places humanity inside loss, and 103:3 describes an excepted community and route out. Their spatial contact lets the root image suggest a protective, life-bearing counter-container around the warning.
findings.reader_payoff: The later enclosure in loss is no longer the only spatial image available in the pericope; the opening can also be felt as a generative enclosure.
findings.containment: The focus uses mercy adjectives, not a noun meaning womb. This is a root-level analogy, not a lexical translation, literal womb claim, or promise of new birth.

epistemic.reason: The reader walks explicitly frame this root-image opposition as exploratory; the focus morphology remains adjectival and the changed reading is analogical.

findings.title: The opening can counterpoint the enclosure of loss
findings.claim: The basmala can carry a life-bearing and overlying protective image against the later placement of humanity inside loss, while the exception supplies a route out of that enclosure.
findings.mechanism: The mercy adjectives carry the r-h-m womb branch, and the opening ism occurrence carries a root-level cover branch. Those focus images meet 103:2's explicit fī khusr enclosure and 103:3's exception. The resulting spatial contrast makes the prefatory formula a possible counter-enclosure without changing the locally selected meanings of name and mercy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a protective opening frame beside the surah's severe enclosure of loss.
findings.containment: The fixed words remain Allah's name and mercy adjectives. Womb and overhead-cover senses are analogical root imagery, not translations of the focus words; the packet does not claim literal rebirth, roof, or a stated causal rescue mechanism.

epistemic.reason: Two unbound reader walks describe the counter-container as exploratory, while the trusted publication source for the same anchors has grade reject. The focus morphology remains name and mercy adjectives, so the analogy is retained with that limitation visible.

findings.title: Reciprocal care gives the kinship and womb images social shape
findings.claim: The repeated exhortation makes the kinship branch of the doubled mercy socially audible, while the womb branch sets that communal exit against humanity's being inside loss; together the exception can be read as reciprocal care leading out of enclosure.
findings.mechanism: The focus mercy adjectives carry both the near-kinship and womb branches. At the far end, two mutual exhortations provide an independent relational operation; 103:2's fī khusr supplies an independent enclosing image. Their contact lets the exception read as a community held together while moving out of loss.
findings.reader_payoff: The exit in 103:3 appears not only as a list of individual qualifications but also as a shared relation within a life-bearing counter-frame.
findings.containment: Kinship and womb are root-level analogies on mercy adjectives, not literal descent or a lexical maternal claim. The verses still name belief, good work, truth, and patience as the exception's content.

epistemic.reason: The bond reading has trusted support, but the combined social/protective relation joins two attributed analogies; the womb support is explicitly exploratory and its prior publication carries grade reject.
